price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: PULL_UP as a counter play type
league-wide consistency threshold (>=70% of units positive, median >2pp)
methodological_questions: How are 'PNR fail', 'unit' and 'lift' defined without using the possession outcome?
What baseline defines lift (the same unit's PULL_UP rate or PPP when the PNR is not suppressed, or the league PULL_UP PPP)?
Can the ≥70% positive and median >2pp thresholds be separated from noise at realistic per-unit sample sizes?
Is any apparent counter lift an artifact of selection, regression to the mean, an outcome-derived label or confounding by player/defense?
Is the result stable out of sample (new season) and against a placebo counter?

historical_evidence.finding: Descriptive star-suppression work. Giannis forced into PULL_UP had PPP 0.848, -0.540 vs his preferred DRIVE, the largest gap. Lineup gaps used n>=30 cells. The record notes no placebo or matching, and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Flagged RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

Descriptive, 25 teams, min 30 poss per cell. Regular season to playoffs, PULL_UP PPP allowed +0.341 with opponent share -7.6pp; PNR PPP allowed -0.139 with share +12.1pp. No inferential test; the PNR share jump may reflect tagging differences. Flagged LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR.

On-ball coverage labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup/PBP fields were labelled at only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of possessions. switches_on was unpopulated. Failed gate; flagged LABEL_ERROR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Within-game adaptation toward 'SHOULD' counter play types showed an adapter advantage of about +0.05 to +0.06 PPP. The SWITCH subgroup reversed, and the no-signal baseline was highest in one test. Limited by selection or regression to the mean.

Falsification of the A1 adapter lift. Wrong-way teams were not worse than no-signal teams, there was no confidence gradient, and no next-game carryover (Welch p=0.842). Flagged LABEL_ERROR, MECHANICAL_FLOOR and selection/RTM.
Raw counter lifts for the TOV_FORCE channel shrank by about 50% or more after adversarial re-routing. Net lift was model-implied, not observed, from 4 games.
Descriptive: PBP-derived shot-level PNR shares vary by team (2024-25, OKC 7.6% to IND 13.8%). Possession-level PNR rates are higher, which shows PNR labelling depends on the definition.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball defensive scheme/coverage from NBA matchup and PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Confident label rate of 3.3% to 14.9%; switches_on not populated; small n. Recorded as A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: A1 adapter PPP lift as a real coverage response
failed_approaches.why: Falsification tests failed (no wrong-way penalty, no confidence gradient, no carryover). Recorded as C_artifact via label error and selection/RTM.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game 'did_adapt toward SHOULD counters' as a PPP improvement
failed_approaches.why: Limited by selection or regression to the mean; subgroup reversal (SWITCH).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Forced-play-type suppression gaps without placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: No placebo; later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record directly tests 'PNR fail then PULL_UP' as a league-wide counter with the stated thresholds.
Earlier counter and adaptation lifts in this project were repeatedly classified as artifacts (FAM:SF13, FAM:SF-APPA-001) or shrank under adversarial checks (FAM:SF-APPA-067).
Coverage/scheme labels from this data are unreliable at the possession level (FAM:SF-APPS-058).

The only PULL_UP evidence points the other way: Giannis forced into PULL_UP scored much less than on DRIVE (FAM:SF-CHT-009), and league PULL_UP PPP allowed rose in the playoffs (FAM:SF-APPS-012). Both are descriptive.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP has a positive lift after PNR failure in any definition of 'PNR fail'.
The distribution of per-unit lifts or the share of units above zero.
Whether any PULL_UP lift survives controls for player quality, defense quality, shot difficulty or regression to the mean.
Which unit definition is feasible or powered, because no retrieved record specifies one.
own_inferences: The conditioning event 'PNR fail' risks being defined from the possession outcome or from the next action, which would build a positive or negative lift into the label.

PULL_UP shots are often taken when the offense is already disadvantaged, so lift against all-possession PPP may be negative by construction; against the same player's unconditioned PULL_UP PPP it may be near zero.

A '>=70% of units positive' rule is weak evidence unless units have enough n. At small n, noise alone gives roughly 50% positive units with wide spread, and a median >2pp threshold needs a real effect plus enough precision.
Because prior counter lifts in this project mostly collapsed under falsification, the prior for a robust league-wide positive lift is low.
uncertainties: The definitions of 'PNR fail', 'unit' (team, player, team-season, lineup?) and 'lift' (pp of PPP, eFG or frequency?) are not given.
Data version: 2025-26 playoffs were partial on 2026-05-23 (complete only from 2026-06-21), so unit counts and sample will change. 2025-26 regular season is complete.
The coverage of the derived play-type graph for PNR and PULL_UP tagging is unknown. FAM:SF-APPS-012 suggests tagging differences.
The retrieved records are on related but different questions, so transfer is uncertain.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history this might have been a straightforward proceed. The records show a repeated pattern of counter-lift artifacts (selection/RTM, label error), unreliable scheme labels, and descriptive PULL_UP numbers that run against the hypothesis. That moved me to proceed_with_changes: require a non-outcome-derived PNR-failure definition, a placebo play type, a holdout season, and a minimum n per unit, and lower the supported probability.

blocking_constraints.text: If PNR 'failure' is defined from the possession result or the subsequent action, the lift is mechanically biased. A pre-outcome definition is needed (e.g., the ball handler cannot create separation, the screen is blown up, or a non-shot reset before the pull-up).
Per-unit counts of failed-PNR-then-PULL_UP possessions may be too small, which would make the share-of-units criterion noise-dominated.
Coverage and failure labelling from PBP/matchup fields has had low confident-label rates (FAM:SF-APPS-058), and PNR tagging varies (FAM:SF-APPS-012).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests this hypothesis. Related work gives descriptive PULL_UP numbers that run against it, unreliable scheme labels, and counter or adaptation lifts that were artifacts or shrank. The question is open but the prior is unfavorable.

risks.text: The failure label for the PNR could be derived from the same outcome as the lift.
Units chosen because they suffered PNR suppression, or counters chosen for strong results, will regress toward the mean (as in FAM:SF13).
Pull-up takers (player quality), defender quality, clock and score state, and shot location all affect lift independently of the PNR failure.
Small units give noisy lifts, so the 70% positive criterion is hard to distinguish from chance.
Failed PNRs followed by a pull-up are a small share of possessions.
Mis-tagging of PNR and PULL_UP in the derived play-type records, and low coverage of defensive scheme labels.
Pull-up PPP and eFG are low relative to other shot types, so a positive 'lift' depends on the chosen baseline.
Without a placebo play type, any lift can come from the baseline construction (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Many units, play types and thresholds raise the false-positive risk for a 'best counter' claim.
Season-to-season changes in league style and tagging, and regular season vs playoff differences.

design.estimand: For each unit u, lift_u = PPP (or eFG, as pre-declared; primary = PPP in pp per 100 possessions /100) on possessions where a PNR was suppressed and the next action was PULL_UP, minus a matched baseline (same ball handler and defense team, other terminal action choices after a suppressed PNR, plus a second baseline of the same handler's unconditioned PULL_UP). Primary claim: share of units with lift_u>0 is >=70% and the median lift_u >2pp.
design.unit: Primary: offensive team-season (n_poss >= threshold below). Secondary: primary ball-handler-season. Units are fixed before looking at lifts.
design.sample: NBA regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 as discovery; 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) as frozen out-of-sample confirmation. Playoffs reported separately and excluded from the primary because 2025-26 playoffs are partial at the posing date. Exclude garbage time and end-of-period possessions.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum of 60 qualifying possessions per unit (to be tuned by simulation on the discovery data) and report the number of qualifying units. Use a simulation with per-unit possession-level SD to give power for a true median 2pp lift and for the 70% share. State a minimum detectable effect; if fewer than about 20 units qualify or power for the median is under 0.8, declare 'underpowered' rather than 'rejected'.
design.controls: Define 'PNR fail' only from information before the shot: screen action recorded, no shot, no foul, and a reset, or a defender recovery tag. Do not use the possession result. Adjust for ball handler, defending team, shot distance, shot clock, score margin and period. Use empirical-Bayes shrinkage of unit lifts, and report the share of units with a shrunken lift >0. Test sensitivity to at least two PNR-failure definitions.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo play types (e.g., DRIVE, SPOT_UP) subjected to the same pipeline: a counter claim fails if the placebo also passes. (2) Permutation test shuffling the failure label within handler-season. (3) Split-half stability within the discovery seasons, then the 2025-26 holdout: the lift must keep its sign. (4) Check the lift against regression to the mean using the prior season's lift as a predictor. (5) Label audit on a sample of tagged PNR/PULL_UP sequences.
design.multiplicity: One primary hypothesis (team-season, PPP, primary failure definition). All secondary units, metrics and failure definitions labelled exploratory; Holm correction for the secondary family. Number of tests logged.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if, in the 2025-26 holdout and the pooled discovery set, >=70% of qualifying units have lift>0, median lift >2pp with a bootstrap (cluster by game) 95% CI above 2pp, the placebo and permutation tests fail to reproduce it, and the result holds under both failure definitions. Rejected if the powered test gives a median CI below 2pp or a share below 70%. Underpowered or label-coverage failure gives untestable/uncertain. Placebo reproduction gives artifact.
design.data_version: Freeze: 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular seasons (full); 2025-26 regular season complete as of 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs excluded from primary because partial on 2026-05-23 (complete from 2026-06-21). Record graph build/tagging version and the extraction date.

research_concepts: pull-up jump shot as counter strategy
unit-level lift in points per possession
methodological_questions: Does PULL_UP show positive lift against PNR-failure/suppression in at least 70% of units with median lift above 2 percentage points?
How are units, lift and the PNR failure condition defined and measured from play-by-play and derived play-type possession records?
Is the pull-up counter effect robust to selection, regression to the mean, sample size and confounding by player or defense quality?
Is a prior threshold-based replication or placebo test of counter strategies available?
args.query: PNR fail then PULL_UP league-wide counter: lift>0 in >=70% of units and median lift >2pp; defensive suppression and counter strategy best/avoid

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
